summary:
Our project, “Abandoned but Not Forgotten,” explores the history of human space exploration from the 1960s to the present, focusing on missions and equipment sent to the Moon and Mars.

Project Description

Through our interactive website, we present information about historical and modern space missions, including spacecraft, landers, rovers, and scientific instruments sent to the Moon and Mars. We highlight their missions, discoveries, achievements, and the equipment left behind on these celestial bodies.

Project Objectives

- To explore the history of Moon and Mars exploration.
- To showcase important NASA missions and their contributions.
- To raise awareness about abandoned space equipment.
- To preserve the stories behind these forgotten technologies through digital storytelling.

Our Solution

We developed a website that allows visitors to explore the Moon and Mars and discover the stories of space missions and equipment left behind. Our goal is to make space exploration history more accessible, engaging, and educational.

Conclusion

Every mission leaves behind a story. Even when a spacecraft stops working, its contribution to science and human exploration remains valuable. Through this project, we aim to ensure that these forgotten machines and their achievements are never forgotten.

details:
1.

Our project is an interactive storytelling website that explores NASA's space missions to the Moon and Mars from the 1960s to the present. It presents information about spacecraft, landers, rovers, and scientific equipment sent to these planets. Users can explore each mission, learn about its journey, achievements, scientific contributions, and the equipment left behind after the mission ended. The website uses visual elements and animations to make space exploration easier to understand.

2.

Our project makes space exploration history more accessible, interesting, and enjoyable for everyone, especially students and young learners. It helps users understand the importance of past NASA missions, discover scientific achievements, and learn how abandoned equipment continues to represent valuable contributions to science. It also encourages curiosity about space exploration and technology.

3.

The main goal of our project is to preserve and share the stories of NASA's space exploration missions and the equipment left behind on the Moon and Mars. We want to show that even when a mission ends, its scientific contributions and historical importance remain. Our project aims to inspire future generations, increase interest in space science, and remind people that every piece of space equipment has a story worth remembering.

4.

We used the following technologies and tools to develop our project:

  • HTML: To create the structure of the website.
  • CSS: To design the layout, colors, animations, and visual appearance.
  • JavaScript: To add interactivity and dynamic features.
  • Visual Studio Code: As our code editor.
  • Web Browser: To test and preview the website.
  • AI-assisted development tools: To support website development, design, and problem-solving.

We used a computer and internet connection as our primary hardware resources.

5.

Our project presents space exploration history through an interactive and visually engaging storytelling experience. Instead of displaying only traditional text and information, we combine space-themed designs, animations, visual elements, and interactive exploration. Users can discover the stories behind different missions and understand what happened to the equipment after its mission ended. We turn forgotten space technology into an engaging journey through history.

6.

While developing our project, we considered several important factors:

  • Historical Accuracy: Using reliable information about NASA missions and space equipment.
  • Educational Value: Making scientific information easy to understand.
  • User Experience: Creating a simple and user-friendly interface.
  • Visual Design: Using space-themed visuals, animations, and attractive layouts.
  • Accessibility: Making information understandable for students and general audiences.
  • Creativity: Presenting historical information through interactive storytelling.
  • Technical Feasibility: Choosing technologies that allowed our team to develop the project with our available skills and resources.
